signature: SUBROUTINE DLAQR3( WANTT, WANTZ, N, KTOP, KBOT, NW, H, LDH, ILOZ,

params.name: wantt
params.reference: If .TRUE., then the Hessenberg matrix H is fully updated so that the quasi-triangular Schur factor may be computed (in cooperation with the calling subroutine). If .FALSE., then only enough of H is updated to preserve the eigenvalues.

params.name: wantz
params.reference: If .TRUE., then the orthogonal matrix Z is updated so so that the orthogonal Schur factor may be computed (in cooperation with the calling subroutine). If .FALSE., then Z is not referenced.

params.name: N
params.reference: The order of the matrix H and (if `WANTZ` is .TRUE.) the order of the orthogonal matrix Z.

params.name: ktop
params.reference: It is assumed that either `KTOP = 1` or $H(\mathrm{KTOP},\mathrm{KTOP}-1)=0$. `KBOT` and `KTOP` together determine an isolated block along the diagonal of the Hessenberg matrix.

params.name: kbot
params.reference: It is assumed without a check that either `KBOT = N` or $H(\mathrm{KBOT}+1,\mathrm{KBOT})=0$. `KBOT` and `KTOP` together determine an isolated block along the diagonal of the Hessenberg matrix.

params.name: nw
params.reference: Deflation window size. $1 \le \mathrm{NW} \le (\mathrm{KBOT}-\mathrm{KTOP}+1)$.

params.name: H
params.reference: On input the initial N-by-N section of H stores the Hessenberg matrix undergoing aggressive early deflation. On output H has been transformed by an orthogonal similarity transformation, perturbed, and the returned to Hessenberg form that (it is to be hoped) has some zero subdiagonal entries.
params.workDependent: the window's Hessenberg reduction and its back-transformation round differently on the blocked and unblocked paths LWORK selects, and the reduction amplifies that in the forward sense

params.name: ldh
params.reference: Leading dimension of H just as declared in the calling subroutine. $N \le \mathrm{LDH}$

params.name: ihiz
params.reference: Specify the rows of Z to which transformations must be applied if `WANTZ` is .TRUE.. $1 \le \mathrm{ILOZ} \le \mathrm{IHIZ} \le N$.

params.name: Z
params.reference: IF `WANTZ` is .TRUE., then on output, the orthogonal similarity transformation mentioned above has been accumulated into `Z(ILOZ:IHIZ,ILOZ:IHIZ)` from the right. If `WANTZ` is .FALSE., then Z is unreferenced.
params.workDependent: the window's Hessenberg reduction and its back-transformation round differently on the blocked and unblocked paths LWORK selects, and the reduction amplifies that in the forward sense

params.name: ldz
params.reference: The leading dimension of Z just as declared in the calling subroutine. $1 \le \mathrm{LDZ}$.

params.name: ns
params.reference: The number of unconverged (ie approximate) eigenvalues returned in `SR` and `SI` that may be used as shifts by the calling subroutine.

params.name: nd
params.reference: The number of converged eigenvalues uncovered by this subroutine.

params.name: SI
params.reference: On output, the real and imaginary parts of approximate eigenvalues that may be used for shifts are stored in `SR(KBOT-ND-NS+1)` through `SR(KBOT-ND)` and `SI(KBOT-ND-NS+1)` through `SI(KBOT-ND)`, respectively. The real and imaginary parts of converged eigenvalues are stored in `SR(KBOT-ND+1)` through `SR(KBOT)` and `SI(KBOT-ND+1)` through `SI(KBOT)`, respectively.

params.name: V
params.reference: An `NW`-by-`NW` work array.
params.workDependent: the window's Hessenberg reduction and its back-transformation round differently on the blocked and unblocked paths LWORK selects, and the reduction amplifies that in the forward sense

params.name: ldv
params.reference: The leading dimension of V just as declared in the calling subroutine. $\mathrm{NW} \le \mathrm{LDV}$

params.name: nh
params.reference: The number of columns of T. $\mathrm{NH} \ge \mathrm{NW}$.

params.name: T
params.workDependent: the window's Hessenberg reduction and its back-transformation round differently on the blocked and unblocked paths LWORK selects, and the reduction amplifies that in the forward sense

params.name: ldt
params.reference: The leading dimension of T just as declared in the calling subroutine. $\mathrm{NW} \le \mathrm{LDT}$

params.name: nv
params.reference: The number of rows of work array `WV` available for workspace. $\mathrm{NV} \ge \mathrm{NW}$.

params.name: WV
params.workDependent: the window's Hessenberg reduction and its back-transformation round differently on the blocked and unblocked paths LWORK selects, and the reduction amplifies that in the forward sense

params.name: ldwv
params.reference: The leading dimension of W just as declared in the calling subroutine. $\mathrm{NW} \le \mathrm{LDV}$

params.name: WORK
params.reference: On exit, `WORK(1)` is set to an estimate of the optimal value of `LWORK` for the given values of N, `NW`, `KTOP` and `KBOT`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The dimension of the work array `WORK`. $\mathrm{LWORK} = 2 \, \mathrm{NW}$ suffices, but greater efficiency may result from larger values of `LWORK`.

If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; DLAQR3 only estimates the optimal workspace size for the given values of N, `NW`, `KTOP` and `KBOT`. The estimate is returned in `WORK(1)`. No error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA. Neither H nor Z are accessed.

notes: no derivable minimum length for workspace WORK

overrides.reason: DLAQR3 hands WORK(JW+1:LWORK) to DGEHRD and DORMHR, which pick their block size from it (DGEHRD shrinks NB or goes unblocked; DORMHR's DORMQR shrinks NB and goes unblocked below NBMIN), as the reference's do (the reference's xGEHRD crossover NX = 128 keeps it unblocked for JW < 128, where the JS NX = 32 does not: ticket 0101). Their blocked and unblocked runs round differently, and returning the reflected window to Hessenberg form amplifies that in the forward sense (the reduction is fixed only by its first column), so the updated H and Z, and the window matrices V, T and WV, differ beyond rounding between the minimum 2*JW and the optimum, while each is an exact orthogonal (unitary) similarity to rounding. NS, ND and the shifts do not depend on LWORK. The module's tests check the minimum WORK past the blocking threshold (JW > 32) against the optimum: the same NS, ND and shifts, and Z^T*H0*Z = H (ticket 0100).

set.params.Z.workDependent: the window's Hessenberg reduction and its back-transformation round differently on the blocked and unblocked paths LWORK selects, and the reduction amplifies that in the forward sense

set.params.WV.workDependent: the window's Hessenberg reduction and its back-transformation round differently on the blocked and unblocked paths LWORK selects, and the reduction amplifies that in the forward sense
